items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: we had a trainer named Tony Sartori who also loved jazz. And I called up Tony

ctx.x: Tell me about some of your most memorable moments in the jazz clubs in Buffalo. I mean is there some night, some artist that stands out in your head?

Oh my God. First time I went to the Bonton on Waverly Street on the east side, it was just like a typical New York or New Jersey bar on a corner. You walk in, there’s a long bar, there’s a back room where you might have a fish fry, etcetera. Well they had put up a little stage this high, so they could get some outlets in. And this seems to be — there was no ad for it, I somehow found out the Three Sounds — Gene Harris and Simpkins and Dowdy were playing. And I was taking piano lessons at the time. And Tom Jones,…

was, and you know Elvin Jones and McCoy, and Jim Garrison and stuff. And I was just doing some interviews of my dear friend who I spent a lot of time with whose name was Paul Gresham. He had a group called Birthright. And a little bit later in his group he had Ricky Ford.
